critical_code_review_comments: server.py:3459 commit_ingestion_records — the roll-up expense from a purchase_bill uses `notes = li_text[:200]` where li_text joins ALL line-item descriptions with spaces (no separator between items). For multi-line bills this loses per-item structure. Consider joining with ' | ' or storing as an array. Cosmetic — data is preserved in the invoice itself.

routers/ledger.py:118 — auto-created Asset from an 'Asset Purchase' expense hardcodes category='Equipment' regardless of what the underlying purchase is (could be a Vehicle, Building, Machinery, etc.). Users then have to open the asset and re-categorize. Consider running the same keyword heuristic (or a lightweight LLM call) on the expense title/vendor to pick the closest ASSET_CATEGORIES value, defaulting to 'Other' or 'Equipment' only if no match. Not blocking but a small UX polish.

routers/ledger.py:242-252 — `PATCH /api/expenses/{id}` silently drops an invalid category (pops it) but keeps the rest of the update. If a client sends an unknown category, they get a 200 with no error surface — safer to 400 with 'invalid category' so bad clients don't silently mispersist a stale value.

routers/ledger.py:279-287 & 309-316 — PATCH endpoints for /assets and /inventory accept the FULL AssetInput/InventoryInput Pydantic model (not a Patch model with Optional fields). This means a client MUST send every field to update just one — a partial PATCH like {"status":"disposed"} on an asset would erase name/purchase_amount/etc. (or 422 depending on defaults). Recommend adding AssetPatch / InventoryPatch models mirroring ExpensePatch (all Optional) for true PATCH semantics.

routers/ledger.py:113-116, 142-145, 162-165 — brain memory row for finance records is inserted directly with `db.memory.insert_one` bypassing any deduplication. Ingesting the same bill twice (or replaying a commit) would create duplicate memory rows for the same expense. Consider deduping on (source, invoice_id/payment_id/expense_id) or delete the prior brain row on expense update/delete. Currently brain search will show stale ghost entries after an expense is deleted.

routers/ledger.py:255-258 — DELETE /api/expenses/{id} does NOT cascade-delete the auto-created Asset (matched by expense_id) nor the brain memory row. After deleting a bill the linked asset+brain memory linger. Minor data-hygiene issue.

routers/ledger.py:326-358 — ledger_summary loads up to 5000 expenses/assets/inventory per call into memory and reduces in Python. For a tenant with high finance volume this becomes O(n) hot path on the dashboard. Move totals/by_category/by_vendor/by_month into MongoDB aggregation pipelines ($group) for scalability.

server.py:3540-3549 — purchase_bill roll-up unconditionally creates an expense on EVERY commit, even if commit_ingestion_records is retried or the same ingestion re-committed under a different id. The commit endpoint DOES block re-file with `status=='filed'` (server.py:3719-3720), so this is protected — but the underlying commit_ingestion_records helper is not idempotent. If it's ever called from a code path that isn't the endpoint (e.g. a future retry job), duplicate expenses will be created. Consider guarding by (ingestion_id, invoice_id) uniqueness.

Ledger.js — three Radix DialogContent elements (Add Expense, Add Asset, Add Inventory) are missing DialogDescription/aria-describedby. Runtime prints an a11y warning every time a dialog opens. Add `<DialogDescription>` inside each dialog for a11y compliance.

Ledger.js Add Asset dialog — the purchase_amount input does not have a data-testid (only asset-name and asset-save do). Adding data-testid='asset-amount' + 'asset-category' (and similar for Add Inventory quantity/unit_cost) would make future regression tests less brittle. Currently the test relied on 'input[type="number"]' selector which is fragile.
action_items: OPTIONAL: Add <DialogDescription> or aria-describedby to the three Radix dialogs in Ledger.js to silence the runtime a11y warning.

OPTIONAL: Convert PATCH /api/assets/{id} and PATCH /api/inventory/{id} to accept a proper Patch model (all Optional) instead of the full AssetInput/InventoryInput, so partial updates don't blank untouched fields.

OPTIONAL: Auto-created Asset from 'Asset Purchase' expense (routers/ledger.py:118) hardcodes category='Equipment' — run the guess_expense_category-style heuristic against ASSET_CATEGORIES for smarter defaults.
OPTIONAL: DELETE /api/expenses/{id} should cascade-delete the linked auto-Asset and the brain memory row (data hygiene).
OPTIONAL: Move ledger_summary aggregation into a MongoDB $group pipeline for scalability (currently loads up to 5000 rows into Python per call).
OPTIONAL: Return 400 (not silent drop) when PATCH /api/expenses receives an invalid category value.
